# The storyboard

The third stop: the script of the whole page, which the person says yes to. Write it to `docs/story/storyboard.md`.

A plan covers what its asker thought to ask for. Most people ask for the idea and for what moves. Nobody asks what the site does on a phone, or without the 3D, or what a shared link shows, and a script that leaves those out is half a script. So this one has a place for each, and an empty place shows.

## The chapters

A row to a chapter:

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## The beats

Under each chapter, a row to a beat. A beat is one settled state of the scene and one block of text.

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **How the pieces stand:** a stack, a fan, a ring, a row, a wall, or what the chapter needs. The same pieces in every beat.
- **What is on their faces:** the person's real pictures and words. Name the picture.
- **What the chapter adds:** anything in the scene besides the pieces. Often nothing.
- **Its caption:** a title and a sentence or two, written from the fact sheet.

A caption says nothing the fact sheet does not say. What a project taught the person, what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used: those are theirs to tell you. Where you want such a sentence and do not have it, write the question in its place.

## Someone with thirty seconds

Say how a visitor who does not scroll gets the name, what the person does, one proof of it, and how to reach them. The first screen carries the first three. A rail jumps to any chapter, and one link skips to the close.

# Storyboard — The Memo

Object: seven memo cards — Atlantico Telecom (churn analysis), the Helix sample tracker, the Helix weekly scheduling report, the Lisbon Rent Map, FraudShield, the Health Data Hackathon, AutoPilot. Flat rectangles with a clipped corner, like a real index card.

## The chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The question | Opening | His name, "I make dashboards people actually use," the site's question | One blank card, tilting into place, question mark resolving into the real question | Scroll; the rail and a "Get in touch" link are already visible, doing nothing yet |
| 2 | Who's asking | Who | Lisbon, product analyst, economics into data science, now looking to move from banking to a product company | The card gains a header — his name and title — while the other six sit stacked, face down, to the side | Nothing new |
| 3 | The data | Where from | The path: Atlantico (2020) → Helix Genomics (2021–24) → DataTugas (2018–20, mentioned not shown) → Meridian Bank (2024–) | The seven cards unstack and lay out along a line, headers only | Drag or scroll-scrub along the line; hover a card for a one-line label |
| 4 | What I did | How | His method, worked through on one real example | The Helix scheduling-report card detaches and unfolds into its five faces: Question, Data, What I did, What I found, What I'd do | Step through the five faces one at a time (click or continued scroll) |
| 5 | What I found | What, and outcomes | The real work, shown | All seven cards fan into a wall, each turning to its real face | Click any card to read it in full; Beatriz Lima's line appears pinned to the Helix card |
| 6 | What I'd do | The close | The question, answered; the ask | The seven cards gather back into one, filed and complete | Email link, LinkedIn link, CV download if supplied |

## The beats

### Chapter 1 — The question

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | 1 | One card, centred, at rest | Blank but for a large "?" | His name set below the card, plain type | "Rafael Costa — I make dashboards people actually use." |
| 1b | 0.5, scroll-tied | Same card, tilting up toward the viewer | The "?" dissolves as the real question types itself on | Nothing else on screen — the card carries it alone | "What makes a dashboard something people actually open?" |

### Chapter 2 — Who's asking

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2a | 1 | The one card centred; six more sit stacked, face down, off to its right | A "Prepared by" line fills in on the lead card | A small portrait circle beside the name, if he supplies a photo; otherwise his initials | "Lisbon. Economics first, then data science at Universidade do Douro — 2017 to 2022." |

### Chapter 3 — The data

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3a | 1.5, horizontal scrub tied to vertical scroll | The seven cards unstack into a single line, oldest to newest | Each shows only its header: employer or project, and year | A text callout beside the line for DataTugas, which has no card of its own | "Atlantico Telecom, intern, 2020. Helix Genomics Institute, 2021 to 2024. A study group of twelve he started at university, DataTugas, 2018 to 2020. Meridian Bank, 2024 to now." |

### Chapter 4 — What I did

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4a | 2 | The Helix scheduling-report card leaves the line and opens into five faces, fanned like a hand of cards | Question / Data / What I did / What I found / What I'd do, each with one real line | A quiet row of tool chips — SQL, dbt, Python, Tableau, Power BI, Statistics — static, not animated | "Question: why do the sequencers keep getting double-booked? Data: the core's own weekly schedule. What I did: rebuilt the report around it. What I found: it was taking five hours to produce, every week. What I'd do: cut it to two — and the clashes stopped." |

### Chapter 5 — What I found

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5a | 2 | All seven cards fan into a wall, at slightly different depths | Each turns to its real face (see below) | Beatriz Lima's line, pinned to the Helix card like a note clipped to it | Per card, below |

Per-card captions in the wall:

- **Atlantico Telecom** (text only, no image exists): "Churn analysis, as an intern, 2020."
- **Helix sample tracker** (a plain, stylised recreation of the panel layout — no real data, pending his yes): "Tracked samples through the sequencing core."
- **Helix scheduling report** (shown as a stat, already opened in Chapter 4): "Five hours to two, every week." With Beatriz Lima's line pinned beside it: *"Rafael's dashboards changed how the core plans its week. He is the reason we stopped double-booking the sequencers."* — Beatriz Lima, Head of the Sequencing Core.
- **Lisbon Rent Map** (his own screenshot): "What a room costs, in every parish of Lisbon. About 3,000 visits a month, his own."
- **FraudShield** (his own notebook or chart image): "An MSc capstone. A notebook, against a public dataset of card transactions. Never ran anywhere."
- **Health Data Hackathon** (his chart from the entry, if he has it; otherwise text only): "Health Data Hackathon, 2023. A team of five — he made the charts."
- **AutoPilot** (text only; Meridian's, nothing more can be shown): "A script that fills in his team's weekly report, from SQL. Six people use it."

### Chapter 6 — What I'd do

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6a | 1 | The seven cards gather back into one, the rest filed behind it | The finished memo: Question (restated), Data, What I did, What I found, What I'd do | Email link, LinkedIn link, CV download if he supplies one | "What I'd do: this, somewhere people are building a product, not just a bank. Get in touch." |

## Someone with thirty seconds

The first screen (1a) carries his name and "I make dashboards people actually use." A rail, visible from the first screen on, jumps straight to any chapter. A "Get in touch" link, also visible from the first screen, skips straight to Chapter 6 — so the fourth thing a thirty-second visitor needs, how to reach him, is one click away without reading anything else. The one thing the first screen does not carry on its own is a proof figure; the rail's label for Chapter 5 ("What I found") doubles as that promise, since the wall is where the real numbers sit.

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | The same six chapters, the same captions, one column. Chapter 3's horizontal scrub becomes a plain vertical list in the same order. Chapter 4's fan becomes a simple five-step stack you tap through. Chapter 5's wall becomes a single-column list of cards, in the same order, each full width. Touch replaces hover for any one-line labels. |
| With reduced motion | Every beat still happens, but as a cut, not a move: cards appear already in their end state for that beat, no tilting, unfolding, sliding or parallax. The scrub in Chapter 3 becomes an ordinary scroll down a static list. |
| With no WebGL | The 3D canvas does not load. Each beat is replaced by one plain, static image of the card's face at that beat, with the same caption beside it — a calmer, flat version of the same six chapters, in the same order. |
| With no JavaScript | The whole page is one ordinary, long HTML document: headings for the six chapters, the same captions in the same order, the per-card text from Chapter 5 as a plain list with real `alt` text on any images, and a plain list of ways to reach him at the bottom. No animation, no canvas — the scene was always decoration over this document, never the document itself. |

## The look and the type

Three looks, each a reading of "a memo" as a material. Rafael scrolls through a built version of each before choosing; this is what each would feel like.

**A — Office memo.** Ground: warm off-white, like real paper (`#F6F3EC`). Ink: near-black (`#1C1B19`). One accent: a stamped clay red (`#B5452B`), used only for the question mark, the live figures in Chapter 5, and links. Card surface: matte, faint paper texture, a true drop shadow — it should look liftable.

**B — Dashboard dark.** Ground: near-black slate (`#14181C`). Ink: off-white (`#EDEFEF`). One accent: a cool teal (`#3FD6C3`), used only on numbers and the active rail dot. Card surface: dark glass, a thin glowing edge — closer to the BI tools he actually uses all day.

**C — Clean report.** Ground: plain white. Ink: graphite (`#2B2E33`). One accent: a single banking blue (`#1E3A5F`), used only for links and the Chapter 6 call to action. Card surface: flat, a hairline border, no shadow — the most minimal of the three, and the one with the least room for error if the 3D is ever thin.

My own lean is **A**, because "memo" as a material means paper, and a stamped accent colour reads as a mark made by hand on a real document, not a UI choice. **B** is the stronger pick if he'd rather the site read like the tools he builds, not the paper he writes on.

Two typefaces: a humanist sans for all the surrounding prose (the captions, the nav, the long-form text) — something built for reading at length, not display. A monospace, typewriter-styled face for anything printed on a card's own face — the memo's five labels, headers, figures — since that belongs to the form, not to the page around it.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | Build — a persistent rail (jumps to any chapter) and a "Get in touch" link, visible from the first screen | Me, as part of this storyboard; his to veto |
| A page for each project | Never — this is a one-scroll site; Chapter 5 is each project's whole showing | Me, by the form this skill makes |
| Every project listed | Build — folded into Chapter 5's wall, not a separate list | Me |
| How to reach them, and a CV | Email and LinkedIn: build. A downloadable CV: build only if he supplies the file | Email/LinkedIn: me. The CV file: his |
| What others say | Build — Beatriz Lima's line, pinned to the Helix card in Chapter 5, not its own chapter (one quote isn't enough to carry one) | Me |
| Languages | Not decided — ask him: English only, or English and Portuguese? | His |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | Build, but needs an asset from him: which image should a shared link preview show — the Rent Map, or the opening question-mark card? | His to pick; mine to build once picked |
| The page for an address that is not there | Build — a blank card captioned "No ticket here," matching the form | Me |
| A blog | Never, unless he wants one — nothing in the material calls for it | Me, default; his to override |
| A chat | Never — no reason for one on a portfolio | Me |
| A legal notice | Build — he's in Portugal, the EU; a plain privacy/contact notice is a legal floor, not a taste call | Me, as a legal necessity |

## What you ask for

A yes to this script, or what to change in it. The decisions made without asking are in `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`, alongside this file.
